title: Activated Microalgae–Activated MLSS Bacteria Consortium Synergistically Improves Phycoremediation Kinetics: A Parallel Bio‐Activation Approach for Effective Wastewater Treatment and Biomass Production
content:
Chlorella vulgaris and MLSS bacteria from secondary sludge were activated separately through starvation techniques, and rapid phycoremediation with improved nitrate uptake kinetics was achieved by synergistic action during secondary treatment of sewage in a high-rate algal pond (HRAP).


ABSTRACT

Rapid and efficient wastewater treatment processes with valuable resource recovery are the need of the hour for developing robust, sustainable, and integrated biological systems. This study introduces a novel parallel bioactivation approach combining Chlorella vulgaris and mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSSs) bacterial consortium for wastewater treatment in an outdoor high-rate algal pond (HRAP). C. vulgaris was activated separately in suboptimal nutrient concentrations (0.1×) with respect to the standard commercial medium for 2 days before treatment. Separately activated bacterial MLSS was incorporated into activated C. vulgaris, making an AM–AB consortium. The AM–AB consortium demonstrated enhanced nutrient remediation with nitrogen removal efficiency of 99.9% after 6-h treatment and complete removal of phosphate (< 0.01 mg L−1) in 2 h of treatment. The maximum specific removal rate for total nitrogen reached 49.81 mg g−1 h−1, whereas ammonia showed high substrate affinity (Ks = 0.53 mg L−1). The consortium achieved 81.73% BOD reduction, indicating the synergistic interaction between microalgae and bacteria, supporting the potential of the AM–AB consortium for biological wastewater treatment.
